Anti-Ragging: ### Anti-Ragging Policy
**Zero Tolerance Towards Ragging**

At MAM School of Engineering, we are committed to providing a safe, respectful, inclusive, and student-friendly learning environment where every student can pursue academic excellence with dignity and confidence. The institution follows a Zero Tolerance Policy towards Ragging and strictly complies with the provisions of the University Grants Commission (UGC) Regulations on Curbing the Menace of Ragging in Higher Educational Institutions, 2009, the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE) Anti-Ragging Regulations, the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Ragging Act, 1997, and all subsequent guidelines issued by the Ministry of Education, Government of India, UGC, AICTE, Anna University, and the Government of Tamil Nadu.

The College firmly believes that every student has the right to study in an environment free from fear, intimidation, harassment, humiliation, discrimination, or any form of physical or psychological abuse. Ragging, in any form, is strictly prohibited within the campus, hostels, transportation facilities, sports grounds, cafeterias, and any location connected with the institution.
### What is Ragging?

As defined under the UGC Regulations, 2009, ragging includes any act by one or more students that causes or is likely to cause physical or psychological harm, embarrassment, harassment, fear, shame, or intimidation to another student, particularly freshers. Ragging may be committed individually or collectively and includes direct, indirect, verbal, physical, psychological, or online misconduct.
Ragging includes, but is not limited to:
â€¢ Physical assault or abuse.
â€¢ Verbal abuse, insults, or offensive language.
â€¢ Mental harassment, humiliation, or intimidation.
â€¢ Forcing students to perform embarrassing or degrading acts.
â€¢ Compelling students to obey unreasonable commands.
â€¢ Restricting the freedom of movement of students.
â€¢ Social isolation or exclusion.
â€¢ Bullying, stalking, or threatening behaviour.
â€¢ Damage to personal belongings.
â€¢ Online or cyber ragging through social media, messaging platforms, emails, or other digital media.
â€¢ Any act affecting the dignity, self-respect, physical well-being, or mental health of another student.
Even an act performed "for fun" or "as an introduction" may amount to ragging if it causes discomfort, fear, humiliation, or harassment

â€¢ Withholding of academic results.
â€¢ Debarring from placement and campus recruitment.

â€¢ Expulsion from the institution.
â€¢ Cancellation of admission.

Grievance Redressal: **Fair, Transparent and Time-Bound Grievance Redressal Mechanism**

At MAM School of Engineering, we are committed to providing a fair, transparent, inclusive, and student-centric academic environment where every student is treated with dignity, equality, and respect. The institution has established a Student Grievance Redressal Cell (SGRC) to ensure that students' grievances are addressed promptly, impartially, and confidentially.

The Grievance Redressal Cell functions in accordance with the University Grants Commission (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023, the guidelines of the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), Anna University, the Government of Tamil Nadu, and other statutory regulatory authorities governing higher education. The institution believes that an effective grievance redressal mechanism strengthens transparency, accountability, student satisfaction, and institutional governance.
The Student Grievance Redressal Cell has been established with the following objectives:
â€¢ To provide students with a fair and accessible mechanism for resolving grievances.
â€¢ To ensure timely and transparent disposal of complaints.
â€¢ To promote justice, equality, and accountability within the institution.
â€¢ To safeguard the rights and interests of students.
â€¢ To create a positive academic environment free from discrimination and unfair practices.
â€¢ To encourage students to voice genuine concerns without fear of retaliation.
â€¢ To continuously improve institutional policies and services through constructive feedback.
Students may submit grievances relating to any academic or administrative matter, including but not limited to:
â€¢ Accessibility for differently abled students
â€¢ Any deficiency in institutional services affecting students
**The Student Grievance Redressal Cell does not ordinarily deal with matters that fall under specialized statutory committees, such as:**
â€¢ Sexual harassment (Internal Committee under the POSH Act)
â€¢ Disciplinary proceedings already under inquiry
Such matters shall be referred to the appropriate statutory committee in accordance with applicable regulations.
The College constitutes a Student Grievance Redressal Committee (SGRC) as prescribed under the UGC Regulations.
The Committee functions independently and follows the principles of natural justice, ensuring that every complainant receives a fair hearing before any decision is made.
The grievance redressal mechanism is based on the following principles:
Every complaint is handled objectively without bias or discrimination.
The institution follows a structured and time-bound grievance redressal process.
Students may submit their grievances through:
Every grievance received is acknowledged and recorded.
The Committee examines whether the grievance falls within its jurisdiction. If necessary, additional information may be sought from the student or concerned department.
Both the complainant and the concerned parties are given an opportunity to present their views. The Committee follows the principles of fairness and natural justice.

After careful examination, the Committee recommends suitable corrective measures to the competent authority. Wherever possible, grievances are resolved within the timelines prescribed under the applicable regulations.
The institution maintains strict confidentiality throughout the grievance redressal process.
â€¢ Identity of the complainant is protected wherever appropriate.
â€¢ Information is disclosed only to authorized officials involved in the inquiry.
â€¢ Students shall not face retaliation for filing genuine grievances.
Every student has the right to:
â€¢ Submit a grievance without fear.
â€¢ Be treated with dignity and respect.
â€¢ Receive a fair and unbiased hearing.
â€¢ Know the status of the grievance.
â€¢ Appeal, wherever permitted under applicable regulations.
â€¢ Submit truthful and complete information.
â€¢ Avoid frivolous or malicious complaints.
â€¢ Follow institutional rules and regulations.
Knowingly submitting false or malicious complaints may invite appropriate disciplinary action.

In line with the UGC Regulations, the institution provides an online mechanism for submitting and monitoring grievances. Students can submit complaints electronically, upload supporting documents, and receive updates regarding the status of their grievance. The College continually reviews and strengthens its grievance redressal mechanism to ensure greater transparency and accessibility.

If a student is dissatisfied with the decision of the Student Grievance Redressal Committee, the grievance may be pursued further in accordance with the provisions of the UGC (Redressal of Grievances of Students) Regulations, 2023, including the appellate mechanism before the Ombudsperson appointed by the University, wherever applicable.

MAM School of Engineering is committed to creating a campus culture founded on fairness, transparency, integrity, and mutual respect. We believe that an effective grievance redressal mechanism not only resolves individual concerns but also contributes to continuous institutional improvement. Every student is encouraged to communicate genuine concerns without hesitation, knowing that they will be heard, respected, and addressed in a professional and timely manner.
By maintaining an efficient grievance redressal system, the institution reaffirms its commitment to student welfare, quality education, and good governance.

POSH Cell: At MAM School of Engineering, we are committed to creating a safe and secure environment for all students and staff, free from sexual harassment.
The POSH Cell has been constituted in accordance with the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013.
• To prevent discrimination and sexual harassment against women.
• To promote a social and psychological environment that raises awareness on sexual harassment in its various forms.
• To deal with cases of discrimination and sexual harassment in a time bound manner, aiming at ensuring support services to the victimized and termination of the harassment.
Any aggrieved student or employee may make, in writing, a complaint of sexual harassment to the Internal Complaints Committee (ICC).
SC/ST: The SC/ST Committee is established to empower the SC/ST students in the institution and ensure that they are provided with a safe and supportive learning environment.
The committee functions as per the guidelines of the UGC and the Government of India.
• To ensure provisions for an environment where all such students feel safe and secure.
• To provide prompt counseling for any emotional emergencies arising on account of any events on the campus.
• To provide a mechanism to redress the grievances of SC/ST students, if any.
• To ensure protection and reservation as provided in the constitution of India.
The committee actively monitors and ensures the effective implementation of the reservation policy in admissions and other programs.
